questions.title: Reasons for not offering phototherapy
questions.text: Can you explain in your own words the primary reasons you don't offer phototherapy to your Non-Segmental Vitiligo patients? Please be as specific as you can; you can list multiple reasons.
questions.routing: Ask Q14 only for those who terminate at Q4.

questions.title: Barriers to phototherapy
questions.text: What are the primary barriers to your Non-Segmental Vitiligo patients receiving and continuing phototherapy treatment?

options.text: My practice does not offer phototherapy in-office
Limited availability of phototherapy providers/centers near patients
Travel burden to get to phototherapy appointments
Time commitment / scheduling demands (e.g., multiple sessions per week)
Cost to patient (e.g., co-pays, out-of-pocket costs)
Patients do not follow through on referrals to outside phototherapy providers
Patients do not perceive enough benefit from phototherapy to justify continuing treatment
Patients perceive phototherapy as inconvenient relative to other treatment options
Patients prefer pharmacologic-only treatment (e.g., topicals, systemics)
Concerns about long-term safety of phototherapy (e.g., UV exposure)
No significant barriers [EXCLUSIVE, ANCHOR TO BOTTOM]

questions.routing: Terminate if Q1_8=1 or Q1_9=1 and Q4_4=0; only allow completes for Q4_4=0 if Q1_2=1 or Q1_4=1.

questions.title: Opzelura use with phototherapy
questions.text: For your Non-Segmental Vitiligo patients currently using the following phototherapy methods, what percentage are also prescribed Opzelura (ruxolitinib)?
questions.routing: Show rows according to Q6_1–Q6_4; enter a whole number between 0–100 in each row.
questions.notes: Percentage response for each displayed method.

questions.title: Phototherapy prescribing before and after Opzelura approval
questions.text: Thinking about your Non-Segmental Vitiligo patients, approximately what percent were prescribed any form of phototherapy (in-office or at-home) in the 12 months prior to Opzelura (ruxolitinib)’s FDA approval? How does that compare to the past 12 months? Phototherapy includes in-office narrow-band UVB, excimer laser, and at-home phototherapy devices.
questions.notes: Two percentage responses for Non-Segmental Vitiligo Patients; range 0–100.

questions.title: Expected change – In-office narrow-band UVB
questions.text: As additional targeted therapies (e.g., oral JAK inhibitors or other novel agents) become available for Non-Segmental Vitiligo, how do you expect your use of In-office phototherapy – narrow-band UVB to change?
questions.notes: Scale from 1 to 7; row randomized; response-bearing row marked candidate.

questions.title: Expected change – Excimer laser
questions.text: As additional targeted therapies become available for Non-Segmental Vitiligo, how do you expect your use of In-office phototherapy – excimer laser to change?

questions.title: Expected change – Prescription at-home devices
questions.text: As additional targeted therapies become available for Non-Segmental Vitiligo, how do you expect your use of Prescription at-home phototherapy devices to change?

questions.title: Expected change – At-home DTC devices
questions.text: As additional targeted therapies become available for Non-Segmental Vitiligo, how do you expect your use of At-home DTC phototherapy devices (non-prescription) to change?

questions.title: Use of Oral JAK Inhibitors with Phototherapy
questions.text: For your Non-Segmental Vitiligo patients, which of the following best describes how you would sequence phototherapy and an oral JAK inhibitor in the future, once approved? Please select one answer only.

options.text: I would start the oral JAK inhibitor at the same time as phototherapy
I would start an oral JAK inhibitor first and then add phototherapy early in treatment
I would start an oral JAK first and add phototherapy later only if response is inadequate
I would start phototherapy first and plan to add an oral JAK inhibitor early in treatment
I would start phototherapy first and add an oral JAK inhibitor later only if response is inadequate
I would generally not use an oral JAK inhibitor with phototherapy
I would not use an oral JAK inhibitor for Non-Segmental Vitiligo once approved
It would depend on the patient / case specifics

General Disclosures. Thank you for taking the time to complete this study today. We are conducting a market research study to understand your opinions about Non-Segmental Vitiligo (VIT). This study should take approximately 10 minutes to complete. Please answer all of the questions to the best of your ability.
ZS, the firm conducting this research, is an independent market research agency and consultancy. The research is sponsored by a pharmaceutical company. ZS complies with all laws that protect your personal information and the following market research codes of conduct: EphMRA, Insights Association, BHBIA, and ICC/ESOMAR.
Compensation for participation in the study will be consistent with what was communicated in your invite email. This compensation is not intended to reward you for use of any products which may be mentioned in the study or induce you to use any such products, but rather to understand your views.
Taking part is completely voluntary and you can withdraw at any time and without giving a reason.

Your anonymity will be protected.
